Based on the provided authoritative legal context for Financial Year 2024-25, here is the analysis regarding claiming a deduction for rent when the House Rent Allowance (HRA) component is not received:

**1. Eligibility for HRA Exemption under Section 10(13A)**
The exemption for House Rent Allowance under Section 10(13A) is specifically tied to the receipt of HRA as part of salary. The validation rules state that the exempt allowance under Section 10(13A) is calculated based on the "HRA as per drop down of salary as per section 17(1)" [C2]. Furthermore, the calculation of the exemption requires the "Actual HRA received" to be one of the limiting factors in the "lowest of the following amounts" test [C4]. If the HRA component is not received (i.e., it is zero), the exemption under Section 10(13A) cannot be claimed because there is no HRA income to exempt [C2], [C4].

**2. Alternative Deduction under Section 80GG**
While HRA exemption is not available without the HRA component, the context indicates the existence of an alternative deduction under Section 80GG for taxpayers who do not receive HRA. The validation rules explicitly mention that if HRA under Section 10(13A) is claimed, a deduction under Section 80GG above Rs 55,000 is not allowed [C1]. This implies that Section 80GG is the relevant provision for claiming rent deductions when HRA is not applicable or not claimed. However, the provided chunks do not contain the specific eligibility criteria, limits, or documentation requirements for Section 80GG, only the validation rule regarding its interaction with HRA [C1].

**3. Regime Specifics**
It is important to note that the HRA exemption under Section 10(13A) is available only if the **Old Tax Regime** is opted [C2]. If the New Tax Regime is selected, HRA exemption is not available, and the taxpayer would rely on other deductions like Section 80GG (subject to its own specific conditions not detailed in the provided text) or other applicable deductions [C1], [C2].

**Conclusion**
If you do not receive the HRA component, you **cannot** claim the exemption under Section 10(13A) [C2], [C4]. You may be eligible for a deduction under **Section 80GG**, as the validation rules distinguish between claims under Section 10(13A) and Section 80GG [C1]. However, the specific conditions and limits for Section 80GG are not detailed in the provided authoritative chunks.
